articleTitle: Inside the Starbucks Float: Customer Prepayments and $222.4 Million in Annual Breakage Revenue
summary: Starbucks receives customer cash before delivering purchases, pays cardholders no interest, and reported $1,751.7 million in combined stored-value-card and loyalty-program deferred revenue at September 28, 2025.​ Its fiscal 2025 disclosures establish $222.4 million in breakage revenue from balances expected to remain unredeemed—not separately measured net profit—while federal gift-card protections and state cash-redemption laws constrain the mechanism.​

entities.name: Starbucks Corporation
entities.role: Issues Starbucks Cards and recognizes customer prepayments initially as deferred revenue, subsequently recognizing redemptions and estimated breakage as revenue.​

entities.name: Starbucks Card
entities.role: Merchant prepayment instrument whose balance earns no interest, has no expiration date, and is not FDIC-insured.

verifiedMetrics.label: Combined current balance-sheet liability
verifiedMetrics.context: September 28, 2025: 'Stored value card liability and current portion of deferred revenue,' compared with $1,781.2 million at September 29, 2024. This is not a standalone measurement of unused gift-card cash; current deferred revenue also includes $177.0 million related to Nestlé’s upfront royalty payment.

verifiedMetrics.label: Stored-value-card and loyalty-program deferred revenue
verifiedMetrics.context: Note 11 balance at September 28, 2025, versus $1,718.7 million at September 29, 2024. Includes unredeemed loyalty Stars as well as card balances; approximately $1.6 billion was current at each date.

verifiedMetrics.label: Fiscal 2025 card-and-loyalty revenue deferrals
verifiedMetrics.context: Complete fiscal 2025 reconciliation, in millions: opening balance $1,718.7; card activations, reloads and Stars earned +$15,245.8; card and Stars redemptions and breakage −$15,199.5; other changes −$13.3; closing balance $1,751.7. Other changes primarily reflect foreign-currency translation. Deferrals include Stars and therefore are not exclusively cash loaded onto cards.

verifiedMetrics.label: Fiscal 2024 card-and-loyalty revenue deferrals
verifiedMetrics.context: Complete fiscal 2024 reconciliation, in millions: opening balance $1,567.5; card activations, reloads and Stars earned +$15,807.1; card and Stars redemptions and breakage −$15,665.1; other changes +$9.2; closing balance $1,718.7.

verifiedMetrics.label: Fiscal 2025 total breakage revenue
verifiedMetrics.context: Calculated sum of $200.4 million in company-operated-store revenue and $22.0 million in licensed-store revenue for the fiscal year ended September 28, 2025. The filing classifies these amounts as revenue, not a separately disclosed after-tax profit measure.

verifiedMetrics.label: Fiscal 2024 total breakage revenue
verifiedMetrics.context: Calculated sum of $187.6 million in company-operated-store revenue and $20.0 million in licensed-store revenue for the fiscal year ended September 29, 2024.

verifiedMetrics.label: Fiscal 2023 total breakage revenue
verifiedMetrics.context: Calculated sum of $196.1 million in company-operated-store revenue and $18.9 million in licensed-store revenue for the fiscal year ended October 1, 2023.

verifiedMetrics.label: California gift-card enforcement payment
verifiedMetrics.context: August 13, 2009 stipulated judgment: $195,000 civil penalty, $20,000 investigative costs and $10,000 cy pres restitution. The case concerned cash or check redemption of balances below $10.00 under the then-applicable law.

verifiedMetrics.label: California mandatory cash-redemption threshold
verifiedMetrics.context: Effective April 1, 2026, California Civil Code §1749.5(b)(2) increased the threshold from less than $10 to less than $15. A specified exception covers donated nonprofit or charitable gift certificates bearing the required disclaimer in at least 10-point font.

deviceA.name: Starbucks Card prepaid-value and breakage mechanism
specs: Customer loads are initially deferred revenue; purchase redemptions subsequently produce revenue. Expected nonredemptions are recognized proportionately as cards are redeemed, using historical patterns and applicable unclaimed-property remittances.

Typical minimum load: $5. Maximum balance per card: $500. Maximum activity per card per day: $2,000. Aggregate daily loads and new-card purchases: $10,000. The agreement permits Starbucks to change these limits without notice.
No activation, service, dormancy or inactivity fees; neither the card nor its monetary balance expires.

Auto-reload can follow a selected date or balance threshold. Preference changes may take twenty-four (24) hours; cancellation must occur at least twenty-four (24) hours before the next scheduled reload. Once loaded, the transaction cannot be reversed under the auto-reload provision.
deviceA.price: Financial scale: $1,751.7 million in combined card-and-loyalty deferred revenue at September 28, 2025; calculated fiscal 2025 breakage revenue of $222.4 million.
deviceA.availability: Documented in fiscal 2025 operations; usable at participating stores, with exclusions including some airport, grocery and bookstore locations.​

coreControversy.corporateClaim: Starbucks presents the card as a convenient payment and gifting instrument that makes customer relationships more rewarding; its annual report also identifies increasing cardholders’ store-visit frequency as a program objective.​
coreControversy.criticismOrAlarm: Customers surrender cash before receiving goods without earning interest, and ordinary balances generally cannot be withdrawn as cash unless law or contractual exceptions permit. This creates an interest-free customer-prepayment float, while expected nonredemptions become revenue; the balance is neither an insured bank deposit nor entirely forgotten money.​
coreControversy.regulatoryOrHistoricalPrecedent: The mechanism is not wholly unregulated: the Credit CARD Act of 2009 establishes a five-year minimum before gift-card expiration and generally restricts inactivity fees unless there has been no transaction for at least 12 months, while states regulate cash redemption and unclaimed property. Starbucks’ August 13, 2009 California judgment required $225,000 in payments, a cash-redemption POS function and employee training; employee procedures had to remain posted until September 15, 2011, POS stickers until March 31, 2011, and customer notices until September 15, 2009.

hiddenCatchesAndLimits: The headline balance mixes obligations: $1,840.6 million is a combined current-liability line, while $1,751.7 million combines cards and loyalty rewards across maturities. Neither is a clean standalone count of unused customer gift-card dollars.

Breakage does not require card expiration or proven individual forgetfulness. Starbucks estimates nonredemption from historical patterns and recognizes it proportionately with redemptions; the contractual monetary balance itself does not expire.​

The $222.4 million fiscal 2025 total is recognized revenue from previously collected value, not newly received cash at recognition and not a disclosed standalone net-profit figure. Calling it 'pure annual profit' confuses revenue recognition with profit measurement.

Cash-out is restricted, but not universally prohibited. California requires redemption below $15 effective April 1, 2026; its law generally exempts gift certificates purchased after 1997 from escheat, with an exception for certificates issued for value that have an expiration date. Starbucks’ accounting separately considers applicable unclaimed-property remittances.​

Auto-reload can replenish the float before a customer intends to spend again: cancellation requires at least twenty-four (24) hours’ notice before the next scheduled reload, and loaded transactions cannot be reversed under that provision. Unused eGifts with the original receipt have a separate contractual refund exception.

avoidAdvice: Do not treat a Starbucks Card as savings: it earns no interest, has no FDIC insurance and generally restricts cash withdrawal.
Do not assume an unused balance expires or must be spent: monetary value does not expire, and California permits cash redemption of qualifying balances below $15 from April 1, 2026.​
fitAdvice: The documented mechanism is customer-financed prepayment plus estimated nonredemption revenue: fiscal 2025 breakage totaled $222.4 million, calculated from the two disclosed revenue categories.

Keep three accounting concepts separate: outstanding card-and-loyalty obligations, annual activations/reloads/Stars deferrals, and annual breakage revenue. The fiscal 2025 figures are $1,751.7 million, $15,245.8 million and $222.4 million respectively; they measure different things.
